chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Umarah narrated to us from his father, saying:

Al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), said: He who denies these four matters does not belong to our Shia: the Ascension, the interrogation in the grave, the creation of Paradise and Hell, and Intercession.

key_terms.الْمِعْرَاجَ: The Night Ascension of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What are the four essential beliefs that define a true Shia according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Sifat al-Shia*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (as) establishing these four beliefs as the definitive litmus test for authentic Shia identity, linking doctrinal fidelity to communal belonging. This narration underscores that acceptance of the unseen—specifically the Mi'raj, Barzakh, and Shafa'ah—is not merely optional piety but a fundamental marker of being 'from our Shīʿah.' It reflects the Imami emphasis on the continuity of divine revelation through the Prophet's ascension and the intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.badr-shahin: Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan (rah) narrated to us from Muhammad b. Umarah from his father that Ja’far b. Muhammad (as) said:
He who denies these four matters does not belong to our Shia: the Midnight Ascension, the tomb's interrogation, the creation of Paradise and Hell, and [the right of] intercession.
